$comment: HP Click 4.10.42 for macOS. Published to HP's file host on 2026-08-26 but NOT listed on their download page, which still offers 4.8.117 -- the file is reachable only by exact URL. Every value below was measured from the real DMG (sha256 9688a6e596e22e5d732c6cf19b7ca4e2f9fc05a0d2e7807e6ae058b9ae4d8118).
$electron_version_source: Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Resources/Info.plist -> CFBundleVersion. NOTE: CFBundleShortVersionString is absent from that plist; read CFBundleVersion. Must match the fetched runtime EXACTLY -- the .node modules are Nan-built, so the ABI is not stable across Electron majors.
$electron_unchanged: Identical to 4.8.117. That is the single most important fact here: the arm64 Electron 39.8.4 runtime ClickGraft already downloads serves this version too, so supporting it needs no new runtime and no new dependency work.

patches.why: HP's crash reporter reads app/package.json: app/main.js does const packagejson=require("./package.json") and passes packagejson.hp_configs.crashAutoSubmit to crashReporter.start as uploadToServer. Left true, every crash dump is sent in plaintext to http://15.23.17.24:9100/upload_crash, or to whatever on the network answers for that address; whether HP's own server accepts connections is unconfirmed -- it did not answer from here on 20 Sep 2026, and on this network neither did addresses that route nowhere, so a connect test from here proves nothing either way. Every ClickGraft release before 1.5.8 set this key on the ROOT package.json, whose copy of it HP's crash reporter never reads (Electron reads that file for its 'main' entry and the version it reports, and nothing else does), so every copy they built went on trying to upload -- found 19 Sep 2026: copies had root false and app/package.json true, a 4.8.117 copy logged 'auto-submit: true', and both its Crashpad dumps were marked upload_count: 1, uploaded: 0, which is an attempt each and not a confirmed upload. verify.py now checks the built value.

Squirrel would otherwise download any newer release HP's feed names (its JSON-file mode version-compares, so it skips an equal or older one). Stock 4.10.42 and 4.11.31 log updates-not-available against today's feed, which names 4.8.118, but a 4.8.117 copy is offered that, and a later feed would offer anything newer: a ~570 MB download and a 'restart to update' bar. The install itself would probably be refused, because the copy's ad-hoc signature is not HP's (inferred), and stock HP's ShipIt dies on a missing Mantle.framework anyway -- but this early return stops the download and the bar. Reached via main.js -> app-starter.js -> require('./app-updater').

HP Click 4.8 and 4.10 write the SNMPv3 user name and both passwords to its log in plain text when the user presses Return in one of the SNMPv3 fields of the printer dialog (credentialsKeyEnter), and that log goes into HP's support and crash zips. HP removed it in 4.11.31; the replacement is HP's 4.11.31 line, verbatim. machan.js carries the same line but is dead code (see $do_not_patch).

ops.anchor: this.log("credentials key enter with - authenticationPassword: "+this.authenticationPassword+" policyPassword: "+this.policyPassword+" userName: "+this.userName)

$patches_verified: Re-measured 19 Sep 2026 on the stock archive: the app-updater and SNMPv3 replace anchors each occur exactly once, and app/package.json has hp_configs.crashAutoSubmit true. constants.js and industries.js are no longer patched here: 4.10.42's index.html loads only jquery.js and bundle.js, so the SyntaxError those ops fixed in 4.8.x cannot happen, and the files are only require()d from node/, which handles them as they are.

$do_not_patch.app/shared/shared.module.js: Dead code -- the live copy is webpacked into bundle.js. An earlier pass half-converted it (rewrote the export, left a top-level import), which is pure noise. Leave it alone.
$do_not_patch.app/machan.js: Dead code -- 242 concatenated module bodies with colliding const declarations; cannot load as a single CommonJS module.

required_dylibs.name: libidn2.0.dylib
required_dylibs.why: The arm64 slice of Dj{Core,Conn}ServicesNative-Electron.node has flat-namespace undefined symbols _idn2_check_version, _idn2_free, _idn2_lookup_ul, _idn2_strerror and ZERO libidn2 load commands. The x86_64 slice has none of them. HP's arm64 build links a curl with IDN support and never ships the library. Flat lookup resolves at CALL time, so the app launches fine and only dies on IDN code paths -- do not conclude from a clean launch that this is unnecessary.

required_dylibs.name: libnghttp2.14.dylib
required_dylibs.why: The arm64 slice of Dj{Core,Conn}ServicesNative-Electron.node has 36 flat-namespace undefined _nghttp2_* symbols from HP's libcurl build with HTTP/2 support. Same class as the idn2 gap: HP links a curl with h2 and ships no nghttp2. nghttp2 is MIT licensed.  NOTE: the formula is libnghttp2, NOT nghttp2. Homebrew split the library out into its own formula; the nghttp2 bottle now contains the command-line tools and no .dylib at all, so fetching it downloads and verifies fine and then finds nothing to extract.
required_dylibs.$measured: ALPN measured 2026-07-31: us1.api.ws-hp.com negotiates http/1.1 ONLY -- an earlier note wrongly cited it as an h2 endpoint. lfp-downloads.hpcloud.hp.com DOES negotiate h2, but that is the updater host, which this patch disables. So no confirmed h2 path is exercised by the patched build today. Bundled anyway because the cost is one small MIT dylib and the failure mode is a hard process abort at call time on any HP endpoint that later enables h2.
required_dylibs.$preload_note: MUST be true. These symbols are flat-namespace ('dynamically looked up'), which dyld resolves only against images ACTUALLY LOADED in the process. Nothing declares a load command for libnghttp2, so with preload:false the dylib sits in the bundle, satisfies an `nm -gU` scan, and is never loaded -- verified with vmmap: libidn2/libunistring/libintl LOADED, libnghttp2 NOT LOADED. Presence on disk is not satisfaction.

$required_dylibs_verified: Re-measured on this build: the arm64 slice of both Dj{Core,Conn}ServicesNative-Electron.node has 36 undefined flat-namespace symbols -- 4 _idn2_* and 32 _nghttp2_* -- matching 4.8.117 exactly. (An earlier draft of this note claimed the 4.8.117 manifest's figure of 36 was wrong because nghttp2 alone counts 32. It was not: 36 is the correct total across both symbol families.)

$not_a_dependency.libmagic.1.dylib: HP already ships this, already universal (x86_64 arm64). Linked by both .node modules, JDFPrintProcessor and goyaApp. Do not copy or replace it.

$unresolved_symbols_note._png_init_filter_functions_neon: RESOLVED 2026-08-27. This fired: importing PNGs crashed the app with EXC_BAD_ACCESS, PC=0x0, LR inside DjCoreServicesNative -- a call through a null pointer. The earlier note called it an accepted, unverified risk and warned that a call site existed; it did. The build now compiles clickgraft/shims/pngshim.c and preloads it, which supplies the symbol as a no-op. That is correct rather than a workaround: libpng installs its portable C filter implementations first and calls this only to override them with NEON versions, so nothing is lost that this build ever had.

$expected_x86_only_note: EMPTY on purpose, and that is a real difference from 4.8.117: HP dropped AdobeAXE16SharedExpat.framework, the orphaned x86-only framework the older build shipped. Everything else still x86-only here is the Electron shell itself (HPClickExe, the four helpers) plus Mantle and ReactiveObjC from Squirrel -- all replaced or made irrelevant by the graft.
verified_by: Measured from the stock DMG, built, verified and PRINT-TESTED on a DesignJet T1600. The PNG crash path was fixed and proven on 4.8.118; this build carries the same shim.
$accepted_unprovided_symbols_note: Carbon Multiprocessing Services, removed from macOS long ago. Referenced by AdobePDFL, libACR, libACRstd, JDFPrintProcessor and DjCoreServicesNative -- Adobe's RIP stack. ACCEPTED, not shimmed: unlike png_init_filter_functions_neon, where a no-op is the correct behaviour because libpng installs C fallbacks first, these return values a caller acts on (a task id, per-task storage). A plausible-looking lie could cause subtly wrong rendering instead of an honest crash. They are equally unresolvable in HP's own x86_64 build, so Adobe's code has evidently guarded these paths for years. Revisit if a crash ever lands with PC=0 and LR inside the Adobe stack.
